::: {.why}
Four days of taxonomy are worth nothing until the store enforces them, and the enforcement has to be a test rather than a convention because you will forget the convention by March.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Rebuild the store so every read path takes an as-of date and a per-source lag, with no path that bypasses either.
- Have a test that fails if any query returns data whose availability timestamp is after the as-of date.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Refactor qlib/store.py so `as_of` is a required argument on every public read function rather than a default. Requiring it is the point: a default is a decision you will stop noticing.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Write tests/test_leakage.py with three tests: every read function rejects a call without as_of, a row inserted with a future availability timestamp is invisible, and the point-in-time universe at a past date excludes a security that first listed after it. Run the full suite.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The store's read interface now requires an as-of date on every path and enforces per-source availability lags, with three tests that fail if a future value becomes visible. This is the foundation the event-driven engine is built on next week.
:::
